attachments.origin_landmark: incisive fossa of the maxilla above the central and lateral incisors, deep to orbicularis oris
attachments.insertion_landmark: mobile part of the nasal septum and the back of the alar part of nasalis (cartilage; the nasal bone is the nearest schema bone: the schema takes a bone id; the true attachment is cartilage/skin and is named in the landmark text)

actions: draws the nasal tip downward and narrows the nostril; assists the dilator part of nasalis by tensing the mobile septum

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population

fiber_architecture.evidence: no measured architecture recorded: no PCSA, fascicle length or force verified from a source for this muscle (Q65 rule: numbers only where a source gives them)

functional_compartments.function_note: Hyperactive depressor septi drops the nasal tip when smiling ('gummy smile' with tip ptosis); a documented botulinum target at the columella base. Present as a distinct muscle in about half of cadavers (Rohrich et al.; not re-verified here).
functional_compartments.source: Standring S (ed), Gray's Anatomy, 42nd ed. (Elsevier 2021), ch. 'Face and scalp' and 'External and middle ear'; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
